approved: Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (Repeal) (No. 1) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would abolish the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission.
It would repeal the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission Act 2012, but would not take effect until a later bill is enacted to set up replacement arrangements.
The bill would also provide transitional rules for transferring records, handling outstanding Ombudsman investigations, and continuing protection for information disclosed under the Act.
Abolishes the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission.
Repeals the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission Act 2012.
Provides transitional arrangements for records, investigations, and reporting requirements.
Charities and not-for-profit organisations that are registered with the Commission.

Defended abolishing the ACNC as part of a red tape reduction agenda that has already cut $2.1 billion in regulation, double the government's target, and said Australia's volunteer workforce, involving more than a third of adults, contributes about $18 billion a year to the economy.

Opposed abolishing the ACNC, reporting the not-for-profit sector generates about $100 billion annually and employs over 900,000 Australians, that over 80 per cent of 155 Senate inquiry submissions supported retaining the commission, and noting the government plans to return regulation to the tax office while cutting 4,700 of its staff.

Defended abolishing the ACNC, describing charities as generating about five per cent of the national economy and one in twelve jobs, and cited her electorate's McIntyre Centre, which raised $50,000 at its 50th anniversary event to support more than 200 young people with disabilities.

Recounted growing his transport business before serving as a Lifeline Central Queensland board member and increasing its turnover by 318 per cent, and argued his business experience showed charities need less bureaucracy, not more, to operate efficiently.
